PAUL PIECZYNSKI,
Appellant

v.

BRIAN SZUMSKI, Sheriff of Luzerne County in his official capacity
__________________________________
items.summary: Pieczynski appealed a federal district court's dismissal of his lawsuit against the Luzerne County Sheriff, in which he sought to void a 2016 sheriff's sale and recover property that had been foreclosed upon by Wells Fargo Bank following his 2013 mortgage default. The plaintiff claimed he possessed an 1812 land patent for the property that he had recorded in 2015, prior to the sale. The Third Circuit affirmed the dismissal, holding that Pieczynski's claims were barred by the Rooker-Feldman doctrine, which prevents federal courts from reviewing state court judgments, and that he forfeited arguments regarding other grounds for dismissal by failing to challenge them in his appellate brief.

items.summary: The order revokes Executive Order 13508 (Chesapeake Bay Protection and Restoration, 2009), stating that the Bay's jurisdictions achieved 100 percent of sediment reduction goals, 90 percent of phosphorus reduction, and 57 percent of nitrogen reduction as of 2025. It directs federal agencies to assess and prioritize funding for direct water quality improvement projects and instructs the Environmental Protection Agency to coordinate with affected states to explore initiatives for environmental health that do not increase costs on residents through stormwater management fees.
items.title: Providing Meaningful Water Quality Improvements Through Collaboration and Oversight of Federal Support

items.summary: The memorandum directs the Office of Management and Budget Director and United States Trade Representative to identify Canadian origin items in federal procurement that can be removed or made non-available for purchase, citing that Canada has imposed barriers to United States companies in its government procurement market while Canadian companies retain preferential access to United States procurement. The Trade Representative is directed to monitor Canadian treatment of United States origin items and inform the President of circumstances warranting further action or restoration of Canadian products to federal procurement availability.
items.title: Restoring Reciprocity in Government Procurement

v.

GARRY LEBRON HAYES,
Defendant-Appellant.
items.summary: The Sixth Circuit affirmed a district court's supervised release condition prohibiting Garry Hayes, convicted of transmitting threatening communications to members of Congress, from contacting any member of Congress during his one-year supervised release period. Although the court found the condition overly broad and acknowledged it burdened Hayes's First Amendment rights, it affirmed because Hayes failed to demonstrate plain error, as the condition's unlawfulness was not obvious or clear. The court noted the condition should have been narrower but found the error did not meet the stringent plain error standard.

items.summary: The Ninth Circuit vacated a district court's denial of qualified immunity to four Anchorage police officers who shot Kristopher Handy as he held a shotgun and advanced toward them during a domestic disturbance response. The court held that Handy presented an immediate threat and that the officers' use of deadly force was objectively reasonable under the totality of the circumstances. The court further determined that the officers would be entitled to qualified immunity because the alleged constitutional violation was not a clearly established violation of law at the time of the incident.

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit held that a motion challenging an amended judgment created through prior collateral relief is not a "second or successive" motion under 28 U.S.C. § 2255 and remanded for further proceedings. Augustin's prior § 924(c) conviction had been vacated and his sentence amended in an earlier successful § 2255 motion, and the court determined that this amended judgment constituted a new judgment that could be challenged for the first time without the "second or successive" gatekeeping restrictions. The court also denied Augustin's request to reassign the case to a different district judge.

items.summary: The Eleventh Circuit affirmed the drug trafficking convictions of two defendants prosecuted under the Maritime Drug Law Enforcement Act for conspiracy and possession of cocaine aboard a stateless vessel in the Dominican Republic's Exclusive Economic Zone. The court rejected their arguments that the statute was unconstitutional as applied to conduct occurring in the exclusive economic zone rather than the high seas, and found no violation of Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure regarding delays in bringing them before a magistrate judge. The case was remanded to correct technical errors in the judgment documents.

items.summary: The bill requires the Administrator of the Transportation Security Administration to develop guidelines to improve returning citizens' access to the Transportation Worker Identification Credential program. The guidelines must assist individuals in custody of Federal, State, and local prisons in preparing applications for TWIC cards and assist individuals requesting appeals or waivers of preliminary determinations of ineligibility. items.summary: The bill amends the Northern Border Security Review Act to require the northern border threat analysis to be updated on September 2, 2026, and biennially thereafter. It requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to update the Department's northern border strategy within 90 days of each threat analysis submission, or notify Congress if no update is needed. The bill also requires classified briefings to Congress within 30 days of each threat analysis and directs the Executive Assistant Commissioner of Air and Marine Operations to develop performance measures for assessing effectiveness at securing the northern border between ports of entry.
items.title: 114 HR 5517 RH: Northern Border Security Enhancement and Review Act

items.opening_verbatim: IB Union Calendar No. 729 119th CONGRESS 2d Session H. R. 7083 [Report No. 119–832] IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES January 15, 2026 Mr. Barrett introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs Septemb
items.summary: The bill amends title 38, United States Code, to improve the Department of Veterans Affairs process for making payments to automobile sellers for vehicles purchased for certain disabled veterans. It requires payments to be processed within 30 days of receiving the final invoice, establishes a centralized office within the Department to handle these payments, and requires tracking of payments more than 90 days overdue. The bill mandates semiannual reports on program administration, requires a Government Accountability Office review, and extends certain pension payment limits to October 31, 2033.
items.title: 119 HR 7083 RH: Centralized Reimbursement for Upgraded Innovative Service Equipment Act

items.opening_verbatim: IB Union Calendar No. 727 119th CONGRESS 2d Session H. R. 7443 [Report No. 119–829] IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES February 9, 2026 Mr. Pfluger (for himself and Mr. Magaziner ) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Commi
items.summary: The bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to realign the mission of the Department of Homeland Security's Office of Intelligence and Analysis to equally prioritize intelligence support to State, local, Tribal, territorial governments and private sector entities alongside support to the intelligence community. It directs the Office to establish forward-deployed intelligence capabilities, facilitate two-way information sharing with fusion centers, and ensure such support does not hinder broader stakeholder responsibilities. The bill requires the Under Secretary for Intelligence and Analysis to report within 180 days on implementation steps, progress on information sharing, effectiveness metrics, and resource or organizational changes needed.
items.title: 119 HR 7443 RH: To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to realign the mission of the Office of Intelligence and Analysis of the Department of Homeland Security, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: IB Union Calendar No. 724 119th CONGRESS 2d Session H. R. 9228 [Report No. 119–826] IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES June 9, 2026 Mr. Onder introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce Septemb
items.summary: The bill amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 to require that contracts between group health plans and network service providers provide plan fiduciaries and designated agents access to all claims and encounter information within 15 days. It specifies that contracts cannot limit access to pricing information, overpayment data, audit capabilities, disclosure of administrative fees, or other claims-related documentation, and requires such information to be provided in standardized data formats. The bill establishes civil enforcement penalties up to $10,000 per day for violations and provides individuals with civil action rights.
items.title: 119 HR 9228 RH: Health Data Access, Transparency, and Affordability Act of 2026

items.opening_verbatim: IB Union Calendar No. 726 119th CONGRESS 2d Session H. R. 9382 [Report No. 119–828] IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES June 22, 2026 Mr. Kennedy of New York introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Homeland Securit
items.summary: The bill requires the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection to link together applications of family members throughout the NEXUS application process within 180 days of enactment. It permits an individual family member to schedule interviews for all linked family members and allows the option of joint interviews. The bill exempts children under 14 years of age from interviews if linked to an eligible family member's application.
items.title: 119 HR 9382 RH: To require the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection to link together applications of family members throughout the NEXUS application process, and for other purposes.

items.summary: This document corrects the interim final rule (IFR) that published in the Federal Register on September 9, 2026. The IFR amends its regulations to permit children born in the United States to “foreign government employees” who are not U.S. citizens to register for permanent residence. DHS also made corresponding changes to Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status and Form G-325R, Biographic Information (Registration). This document will restore regulatory language that was unintentionally removed in the September 9, 2026 IFR, with certain conforming edits.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-8810; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-01847-T] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited (Type Certificate P
items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited (Type Certificate Previously Held by Bombardier, Inc.) Model DHC-8-401 and DHC-8-402 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report that instructions for fay, fillet, and rivet dome sealing were omitted for a bracket installed on the inboard surface of the tank rib, which could allow fuel to leak from the wing fuel tank into the wing dry bay. This proposed AD would require a detailed visual inspection of the affected bracket assembly for signs of fuel leakage and for the presence of fillet seal and fastener dome seal, and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited (Type Certificate Previously Held by Bombardier, Inc.) Airplanes

items.opening_verbatim: COMMODITY FUTURES TRADING COMMISSION 17 CFR Part 165 RIN 3038-AF74 Whistleblower Award Determination AGENCY: Commodity Futures Trading Commission. ACTION: Final rule. SUMMARY: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (“Commission” or “CFTC”
items.summary: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (“Commission” or “CFTC”) is amending its rules implementing section 23 of the Commodity Exchange Act (“CEA”). Section 23 of the CEA and the Commission's implementing regulations provide for the payment of awards, subject to certain limitations and conditions, to whistleblowers who provide the Commission with information that aids in successful enforcement efforts. The Commission is adopting amendments, which are modeled on a similar provision in the Securities and Exchange Commission's (“SEC”) regulations, to part 165 of its regulations to increase the efficiency, transparency, and predictability of whistleblower claims process, thereby protecting and enhancing the program's effectiveness in incentivizing whistleblowers to report. The amendments also include technical corrections to the whistleblower rules to reflect the Whistleblower Office's (“WBO”) move in 2025, consistent with its adjudicatory functions, to the Office of the General Counsel (“OGC”).
items.title: Whistleblower Award Determination

items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or the Agency) is proposing to approve Indiana's Coal Combustion Residuals (CCR) partial permit program under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA). After reviewing the CCR permit program application submitted by the Indiana Department of Environmental Management (IDEM), EPA has preliminarily determined that Indiana's CCR permit program meets the standard for partial approval under RCRA. If approved, Indiana's CCR permit program will operate in lieu of the Federal CCR program, with the exception of the specific provisions noted below. EPA is seeking comment on this proposal during a 60-day public comment period and will hold a hybrid in-person and online public hearing on EPA's preliminary approval of Indiana's partial CCR permit program.
items.title: Indiana: Approval of State Coal Combustion Residuals Permit Program

items.summary: The President continues the national emergency declared on September 23, 2001, with respect to persons who commit, threaten to commit, or support terrorism, as strengthened by Executive Order 13886 of September 9, 2019. The continuation extends the emergency measures for one additional year beyond September 23, 2026, based on the determination that such persons continue to pose an unusual and extraordinary threat to U.S. national security, foreign policy, and economy. This notice is published in accordance with the National Emergencies Act.

The data must be standardized, updated at least twice annually with some data in real time, and organized for public accessibility while excluding sensitive cultural and commercial information. The law directs coordination with federal agencies, states, Indian Tribes, and other stakeholders to ensure data compatibility and interoperability.
